summary_table.title: Payer Policy Summary
summary_table.subtitle: Inpatient chemotherapy is emerging as a focused oncology cost driver

rows.inpatient_bundling_rule: Facility inpatient ancillary supplies, administration, and incidental items are bundled, not separately reimbursed.
rows.site_of_care_restriction: Separate reimbursement limited in facility/inpatient settings; office allowed, home infusion requires precertification.

rows.inpatient_bundling_rule: Facilities cannot separately bill bundled items on same-day services tied to facility fees/procedures.
rows.site_of_care_restriction: Restricted for facility billing with same-day room/facility fee and non-administration procedures.

rows.inpatient_bundling_rule: Bundled into the facility fee when billed on the same date of service.
rows.site_of_care_restriction: Applies to inpatient/outpatient facilities when same-day room/facility fees or administration services are billed.

rows.inpatient_bundling_rule: Routine services, including chemotherapy administration, are bundled into inpatient hospital charges without separate reimbursement.
rows.site_of_care_restriction: Routine inpatient/outpatient facility services, including medication administration, are bundled into facility charges.

reimbursement_policies.evidence: The policy includes chemotherapy within pharmacy and infusion services, but it does not create a DRG-specific chemotherapy payment rule. In facility and inpatient settings, administration charges, routine supplies, and equipment are generally bundled into the primary service; separate reimbursement is limited when the infusion or injection is the primary reason for the facility visit.

utilization_limits: one blood transfusion fee per outpatient setting
provider_role_restrictions: health care professional in facility setting
professional pharmacy services not separately reimbursed
exemptions: patients less than 1095 days of age for J7050

reimbursement_policies.evidence: For facility claims, chemotherapy administration and infusion drug administration are treated as bundled services when reported with a room or facility fee on the same date of service. Separate reimbursement is not allowed for always-bundled services and supplies, and listed chemotherapy-related items are included in the facility payment rather than paid separately.

pairing_conditions: same claim as room or facility fee
exemptions: provider, state, federal contract, and/or requirements indicate otherwise

reimbursement_policies.evidence: The authoring health plan generally bundles chemotherapy administration into facility reimbursement and denies separate payment on the same date of service as a room or facility fee, with state and contract exceptions.

reimbursement_policies.policy_title: Hospital Inclusive Charges Policy, Facility - Reimbursement Policy - UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange
reimbursement_policies.evidence: The policy bundles routine hospital facility services into room and board or facility reimbursement; chemotherapy administration and related routine nursing or IV services are not separately reimbursable.

recommended_action.description:
Recommendation 1: Bundle 96360-96379, 96401, 96402, 96409-96425, 96521-96523, and G0498 when billed on the same date of service / same claim form by a facility provider in the inpatient setting with a room or facility fee or primary medical/surgical service, to curb California inpatient chemotherapy overpayment. Exempt: Contract or federal overrides, CO chemo administration, CO infusion drug administration, KY treatment room exception, WI chemo administration, VA not subject. Peer: Cigna and Elevance internal already bundle 96521-96523 in facility/inpatient settings, and both Elevance policies document same-date bundling..

Recommendation 2: Apply a UB-04 / hospital inclusive-charge bundling edit so revenue codes 270, 279, 300, 309, 361, 391, 410, 412, and 460, plus facility chemotherapy families 025X, 026X, 0270-0273, 0279, 029X, 039X, 045X, 0623-0624, and 063X, are not separately reimbursed on the same claim for inpatient facility reimbursement. Exempt: provider, state, federal contract, and/or requirements indicate otherwise.
